name: tracker-recurring-recovery
goal: Recover recurring wakes and job receipts across an interrupted tick while keeping the occurrence history readable by the pinned legacy runner.

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: A failed enqueue must retain the stable wake identity after an atomic catch-up. After a lost job reply, a reopened worker must adopt the original receipt and update history and last result once.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: The baseline parsed cron but did not exercise occurrence recovery or job adoption. The initial recurring service method cases use SQLite, a fixed clock and injected job and queue ports.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Test-only replay at 39455d3bc3 uses the identical tree as historical 47c58605c4. Both cases failed: the recurring tick and box_jobs schema were absent. Checkpoint c587357de5e6.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: Advance occurrence history, due and durable intent in one SQLite transaction. Recover stable wake requests and claimed job receipts after interruption.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: The same two method cases passed at 7f1476c995, byte-identical to the historical fix tree at 0dd6bd9393. Checkpoint 3fb15d1fada7.

steps.title: Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
